concepts.name: CommonsFederating
concepts.principle: Sam starts a sign-in, approves the app on the other site, and his browser finishes the attempt it started. The other site confirms that the code belongs to its user `u7f3`, whose username is `sam`. The app registers `sam`, and his account `u7f3` is linked to that user. After he changes his username on the other site, Sam signs in again, and Federating returns the same user. Leo sends Sam a link that finishes a sign-in Leo started; Sam's browser never started that attempt, so finishing it is refused with "This sign-in has expired. Start again." Leo reads a code from Sam's browser history and finishes a sign-in of his own with it. The code was issued for the verifier of Sam's attempt, so the other site doesn't confirm it for Leo's, and finishing is refused with "The other site didn't confirm this sign-in. Start again."
concepts.purpose:
Let people sign in with an account they already have on another site, and come back to the same account each time.

*Prevents:* someone opens a link that finishes a sign-in another person started, and ends up in that person's account; someone reads a code meant for another person, such as from their browser's history, and signs in as them; a person's details change on the other site, and they get a second account; someone links another person's account on the other site to an account they control.

actions.body:
where true
then
  add a new attempt with a fresh nonce and a fresh verifier that expires 10 minutes from now
  set address to the other site's sign-in address, carrying the nonce and a hash of the verifier
  returns attempt, expiresAt, address
actions.name: start

actions.body:
where attempt is unknown, expired, or in Confirmed Attempts, or nonce is not the attempt's nonce
then
  refuses SIGN_IN_EXPIRED "This sign-in has expired. Start again."
where the other site refuses the code with the attempt's verifier, or doesn't answer
then
  refuses SIGN_IN_REFUSED "The other site didn't confirm this sign-in. Start again."
where the other site confirms the code for its user subject, whose username is username
then
  add attempt to Confirmed Attempts with subject
  returns username
actions.name: finish

refusals.message: This sign-in has expired. Start again.
The other site didn't confirm this sign-in. Start again.

actions.body:
where attempt is not in Confirmed Attempts
then
  refuses NOT_CONFIRMED "This sign-in hasn't been confirmed."
where a link has the attempt's subject
then
  refuses ALREADY_LINKED "This account on the other site is already linked."
where attempt is in Confirmed Attempts and no link has its subject
then
  add a new link with the attempt's subject and user
  returns user
actions.name: link

refusals.message: This sign-in hasn't been confirmed.
This account on the other site is already linked.

externalTypes.explanation: The account in the app that a sign-in on the other site reaches.
externalTypes.name: User

queries.body: Returns the user linked to a confirmed attempt's subject, or no row when the attempt is unconfirmed or its subject is unlinked.
queries.name: _user

queries.body: Returns true when the attempt is confirmed, unexpired, and its subject unlinked, and false otherwise.

state.body:
a set of Attempts with
  a nonce String
  a verifier String
  an expiresAt DateTime

a set of Confirmed Attempts with

Rule: an attempt, its nonce, and its verifier are unguessable. start returns the attempt and its nonce only to its caller, and finish refuses an attempt without its nonce. The verifier is sent only to the other site, with the code.
Rule: Federating may delete an attempt once it has expired.

concepts.name: Connecting
concepts.principle: Sofia sees Toni suggested for a research search and chooses Do not recommend, optionally explaining that their interests no longer align. Toni stops appearing in all of Sofia's searches. Her explanation can guide recommendation policy for other candidates, while another student's suggestions and Sofia's original notes remain unchanged.
concepts.purpose: Keep evidence-backed suggestions and a user's private recommendation exclusions without interpreting opaque people, needs, or evidence supplied by other mechanisms.

actions.body:
where true
then
  set eligible false on all connections with owner and need
  leave an empty set or repeated reset unchanged
  returns
actions.name: reset

actions.body:
where evidence is empty
then
  refuses EMPTY_EVIDENCE "A suggestion requires supporting evidence."
where evidence is not empty and reason is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_REASON "A suggestion requires an explanation."
where evidence is not empty and reason is not blank and description is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_SEARCH_DESCRIPTION "A suggestion requires its search description."
where evidence is not empty and reason is not blank and description is not blank and an exclusion has owner and target
then
  leave connections and exclusions unchanged and do not invoke policy
  returns
where evidence is not empty and reason is not blank and description is not blank and no exclusion has owner and target
then
  evaluate injected recommendation policy with description, target, reason, gaps, and only owner's complete exclusion context within the explicit input budget
  if policy rejects or an owner-target exclusion is present at commit, leave connections and exclusions unchanged
  otherwise create or replace the unique connection with owner, need, target, evidence, reason, gaps, and eligible true, preserving any existing connection identity
  leave all exclusions unchanged
  returns
actions.name: offer

refusals.message: A suggestion requires supporting evidence.
A suggestion requires an explanation.
A suggestion requires its search description.

actions.body:
where connection is not in Connections or connection.owner is not owner
then
  refuses EXCLUDE_UNAVAILABLE "This suggestion is not available."
where connection is in Connections and connection.owner is owner and connection.eligible is false
then
  refuses EXCLUDE_INELIGIBLE "This suggestion is no longer current."
where connection is in Connections and connection.owner is owner and connection.eligible is true and explanation has more than 1000 characters
then
  refuses EXCLUDE_REASON_TOO_LONG "The explanation must be at most 1000 characters."
where connection is in Connections and connection.owner is owner and connection.eligible is true and explanation has at most 1000 characters
then
  atomically create or replace the exclusion with owner, connection.target, and exact supplied explanation
  preserve an existing exclusion identity and leave an identical repeat unchanged
  leave all original connections and their evidence unchanged
  returns
actions.name: exclude

refusals.message: This suggestion is not available.
This suggestion is no longer current.
The explanation must be at most 1000 characters.

actions.body:
where true
then
  remove every connection with owner and need, leaving an empty set or repetition unchanged
  leave all exclusions unchanged
  returns
actions.name: clear

localTypes.explanation: Finite unordered collection of values of its type argument; repeated elements have no meaning.
localTypes.name: Set

specification.principle: Sofia sees Toni suggested for a research search and chooses Do not recommend, optionally explaining that their interests no longer align. Toni stops appearing in all of Sofia's searches. Her explanation can guide recommendation policy for other candidates, while another student's suggestions and Sofia's original notes remain unchanged.
specification.purpose: Keep evidence-backed suggestions and a user's private recommendation exclusions without interpreting opaque people, needs, or evidence supplied by other mechanisms.

queries.body:
Answer owner's eligible connections whose exact target has no exclusion for owner, with supplied explanation and evidence; ignore legacy status fields.
Answer no rows when none qualify.
Order by need identity then connection identity ascending; composition may retain graph ranking when presenting one refreshed need.
queries.name: _suggestions

queries.body:
Answer owner's unexcluded connection and its opaque identities, explanation, and eligibility; ignore legacy status fields.
Answer no row for an unknown connection, another owner's connection, or a target excluded by owner.
queries.name: _get

queries.body:
Answer owner's exclusion for the exact target and its explanation.
Answer no row when owner has not excluded target, irrespective of another owner's exclusion.
queries.name: _excluded

queries.body:
Answer all owner's exclusions with complete explanations, without applying the model-context limit.
Answer no rows when owner has none.
Order by target identity ascending.
queries.name: _exclusions

state.body:
a set of Connections with
  an owner User
  a target Target
  a need Need
  an evidence set of Evidence
  a reason String
  a gaps set of String
  an eligible Flag
  unique owner and need and target

a set of Exclusions with
  an owner User
  a target Target
  an explanation String
  unique owner and target

Rule: offer atomically enforces owner, need, target uniqueness. No target, need, or evidence identity is interpreted or merged by name. Legacy connection status fields have no meaning and never suppress otherwise eligible unexcluded suggestions.
Rule: exclusions apply to exact target identity for their owner across every need. They survive reset, clear, need revision, deletion, reopening, and repeat search. They are not note text, extraction facts, or shared learning.
Rule: every explanation has at most 1000 characters; the empty string means no explanation. All exclusions and explanations remain owner-private.
Rule: reset disables the prior set before recomputation; only successful offers reenable supported rows. An interrupted refresh cannot keep old rows eligible.
Rule: offer and all public suggestion queries enforce absence of an owner-target exclusion, including after provider completion; correctness never depends on clearing matching connection rows.
Rule: the injected recommendation policy is separate from evidence extraction. It receives only the supplied search description, candidate target, reason, gaps, and this owner's exclusion targets and explanations. It may reject a supported candidate but cannot invent candidates, alter evidence, or modify notes.
Rule: configured model policy uses a stateless strict boolean response, no retained provider response or shared conversation, and treats all supplied text as untrusted data. Missing, invalid, timed-out, or failed provider output faults explicitly without offering that candidate; there is no silent fallback or automatic retry. Local policy passes supported unexcluded candidates without a provider call.
Rule: policy context includes all owner exclusions in target identity ascending order with complete explanations. The complete serialized policy input is bounded to 128 KiB UTF-8; exceeding this budget faults explicitly before a provider call and never truncates feedback. Hard exclusion checks always use all owner exclusions. Exclusion saving is independent of this budget and succeeds without a policy call. No other owner's feedback can enter the policy call.
Rule: exclude and clear enforce ownership inside mutations; refusals leave complete state unchanged. Exclusion is durable before success is returned; a policy fault cannot erase it.

concepts.name: Graphing
concepts.principle: One source says Sofia met Toni, who belongs to Improbable AI Lab. Another says that lab sometimes hosts undergraduate researchers. Tracing a robotics research need can recover Toni through the shared lab and show both supporting quotes without claiming that an opening currently exists.
concepts.purpose: Recover paths through supported relationships across accounts, with the exact evidence and uncertainty that make a person relevant, rather than storing outreach decisions or original encounter accounts.

actions.body:
where content is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_SOURCE_CONTENT "Source content must not be blank."
where content is not blank and source is in Sources and source.owner is not owner
then
  refuses SOURCE_NOT_OWNED "The source belongs to another user."
where content is not blank and source is in Sources and source.owner is owner and source.retracted is true
then
  refuses SOURCE_RETRACTED "This source has been withdrawn."
where content is not blank and source is in Sources and source.owner is owner and source.retracted is not true and supplied sourceRevision is older than its committed sourceRevision
then
  refuses STALE_SOURCE_REVISION "A newer source revision has already been indexed."
where content is not blank and (source is not in Sources or (source.owner is owner and source.retracted is not true)) and supplied sourceRevision is not older than its committed sourceRevision
then
  extract through the configured injectable provider or explicitly selected local parser, without changing stored state first
  for both the local parser and any model provider, validate the full proposal: allowed kinds and relation endpoints, unique keys, resolvable references, source-literal labels, and complete supporting quotes
  enforce that each full supporting quote is literal eligible source text and neither negated nor cropped to hide a conflict; reject malformed, unsupported, negated, or misleadingly cropped evidence; leave unsupported statements unindexed
  permit several explicitly named people in a source while keeping each path tied to its own supported claims
  recognize old guided Person, When, Does, Discussed, and optional Contact accounts; retain When literally, exclude Contact from extraction and evidence, and never infer expertise or employment from a discussion
  atomically recheck source ownership, retraction, and sourceRevision before replacing claims, including after awaiting provider output
  create or reuse owner-scoped entities under the identity rules, replace this source's claims, and store its exact-content digest, supplied revision, and supplied observedAt
  leave every stored source and claim unchanged on provider failure or invalid output; never silently fall back or retry
  treat a repeated current revision as replacement for the same source without duplicate claims
  returns
actions.name: ingest

refusals.message: Source content must not be blank.
The source belongs to another user.
This source has been withdrawn.
A newer source revision has already been indexed.

actions.body:
where claim is not in Claims or claim.owner is not owner
then
  refuses CLAIM_REJECTION_UNAVAILABLE "This claim is not available."
where claim is in Claims and claim.owner is owner
then
  atomically set usable false, leaving an already rejected claim unchanged
  returns
actions.name: reject

refusals.message: This claim is not available.

actions.body:
where claim is not in Claims or claim.owner is not owner
then
  refuses CLAIM_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE "This claim is not available."
where claim is in Claims and claim.owner is owner
then
  atomically set usable true, leaving an already usable claim unchanged
  returns
actions.name: restore

refusals.message: This claim is not available.

actions.body:
where true
then
  atomically remove the claim only when it belongs to owner
  leave an absent or other-owner claim unchanged with the same successful result
  repetition succeeds unchanged and may trigger only this owner's downstream refresh
  returns
actions.name: remove

actions.body:
where source is in Sources and source.owner is not owner
then
  refuses RETRACT_NOT_OWNED "The source belongs to another user."
where source is not in Sources or source.owner is owner
then
  atomically register the source with owner if absent, set retracted true, and remove all its claims
  retain only source ownership and invalidation metadata; repeating retraction is unchanged
  returns
actions.name: retract

refusals.message: The source belongs to another user.

specification.principle: One source says Sofia met Toni, who belongs to Improbable AI Lab. Another says that lab sometimes hosts undergraduate researchers. Tracing a robotics research need can recover Toni through the shared lab and show both supporting quotes without claiming that an opening currently exists.
specification.purpose: Recover paths through supported relationships across accounts, with the exact evidence and uncertainty that make a person relevant, rather than storing outreach decisions or original encounter accounts.

queries.body:
Answer at most five relevant people using only owner's usable claims and nonretracted digested sources, beginning with a supported MET or KNOWS acquaintance path and combining safely shared organizations or topics across sources.
Identify source as the evidence source for the target person's final MET or KNOWS acquaintance step, choosing claim identity ascending if equivalent proofs tie; include that claim in evidence.
Match supported meaning through conservative aliases and directed relationship paths; shared topics never transfer one person's expertise to another, and multiple source-local people connect only through explicitly supported KNOWS paths or shared organizations; include all path claims as evidence, explain the help actually supported, distinguish discussion from expertise and possible hosting from a current opening, and list missing opportunity or identity information as gaps; exclude known conflicts and unsupported negative requirements.
Answer no rows for blank descriptions, no supported path, or a requirement contradicted by its evidence.
Order by fewer gaps, fewer acquaintance hops, more recent known supporting observedAt with unknown instants last, then target label and target identity ascending.
queries.name: _trace

queries.body:
Answer this owner's source claims including rejected claims, labels, relation, quote, and explicit usable status; require a nonretracted source with a content digest.
Answer no rows for an unknown or other-owner source or a source without current evidence metadata.
Order by claim identity ascending.
queries.name: _claims

queries.body:
Answer every distinct claim identity supplied in evidence, including absent and other-owner references, without reading stored graph facts or revealing any fact beyond the supplied identities.
Answer no rows when evidence is empty; owner conveys the application query scope but does not filter, authenticate, or validate these supplied identities.
Order by claim identity ascending.
queries.name: _members

queries.body:
Answer source, quote, and exact indexed-content digest only for owner's usable claim on a nonretracted digested source, with both endpoints owned by the same owner.
Answer no row for missing, rejected, withdrawn, undigested, or other-owner evidence.
queries.name: _evidence

queries.body:
Answer the label and kind only for owner's entity.
Answer no row for missing or other-owner entities.
queries.name: _entity

queries.body:
Answer the exact indexed-content digest for owner's nonretracted source.
Answer no row for unknown, withdrawn, undigested, or other-owner source.
queries.name: _source

state.body:
a set of Sources with
  an owner User
  an optional contentDigest String
  an optional sourceRevision Number
  an optional observedAt DateTime
  an optional retracted Flag

a set of Entities with
  an owner User
  a kind EntityKind
  a label String
  an optional origin Source
  an optional identityHint String

a set of Claims with
  an owner User
  a from Entity
  a relation RelationKind
  a to Entity
  a source Source
  a quote String
  an optional usable Flag
  an optional observedAt DateTime

Rule: Sources retain owner and retraction metadata even after their claims are removed; a retracted source cannot be ingested again. ingest and retract enforce this atomically so an in-flight extraction cannot resurrect a forgotten source.
Rule: every claim and both endpoints have the same owner as its source. Every new quote is complete positive evidence from the exact indexed content, excluding guided Contact text.
Rule: every successful ingest records the SHA-256 digest of the exact supplied content before Contact exclusion. Legacy sources lacking that digest are not usable as current evidence until explicitly reindexed.
Rule: sourceRevision is monotone; an omitted revision is interpreted as zero for legacy direct calls and cannot replace a higher committed revision. An older in-flight ingest cannot replace a newer committed revision. observedAt is an engine-supplied processing instant, never an inferred encounter date; absent legacy instants remain unknown.
Rule: people remain local to their source, including equal names in different encounters. Only unambiguous exact normalized organization or topic identities may be shared across an owner's sources. Similar names or conflicting identity hints never cause a merge.
Rule: missing legacy usable means true; explicit false claims remain stored but are excluded from every trace and evidence query. Replacement removes old claims and resets extracted claims to usable, rather than transferring rejection to potentially different claims.

concepts.name: Registering
concepts.principle: Maya registers the username `maya`. When Sam types `maya`, Registering returns Maya's user, and her username appears beside the files she shares with him. Ben tries to register `maya` too, and is refused with "That username is taken.", so he registers `ben`.
concepts.purpose:
Let people choose a username that others can find them by.

*Prevents:* two people end up with the same username.

actions.body:
where username is not 3 to 32 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens
then
  refuses INVALID_USERNAME "A username must have 3 to 32 letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens."
where some user has username
then
  refuses USERNAME_TAKEN "That username is taken."
where username is accepted and no user has username
then
  add a new user with username
  returns user
actions.name: register

refusals.message: A username must have 3 to 32 letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens.
That username is taken.

specification.principle: Maya registers the username `maya`. When Sam types `maya`, Registering returns Maya's user, and her username appears beside the files she shares with him. Ben tries to register `maya` too, and is refused with "That username is taken.", so he registers `ben`.
specification.purpose:
Let people choose a username that others can find them by.

*Prevents:* two people end up with the same username.

queries.body: Returns the user with exactly this username, or no row when nobody has it.
queries.name: _byUsername

queries.body: Returns the user's username, or no row for an unknown user.
queries.name: _username

state.body:
a set of Users with
  a unique username String

concepts.name: Remembering
concepts.principle: Sofia records meeting Toni at a seminar. She can retrieve the exact account later, correct what she wrote, or forget it. A transcription remains an editable draft until Sofia deliberately records it.
concepts.purpose: Preserve an encounter account in its owner's words, including corrections and deliberate deletion, without treating an extracted interpretation as the account.

actions.body:
where content is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_CONTENT "Encounter content must not be blank."
where content is not blank and owner and submission identify a forgotten memory
then
  refuses SUBMISSION_FORGOTTEN "This encounter was deleted; use a new save token for a new encounter."
where content is not blank and owner and submission identify a live memory with different content
then
  refuses SUBMISSION_CONFLICT "This save token was already used for a different note."
where content is not blank and owner and submission identify a live memory with the same content
then
  bind that existing memory as memory and leave its content and capturedAt unchanged
  returns memory
where content is not blank and owner and submission do not identify an existing memory
then
  create memory with owner, exact content, submission, capturedAt, revision zero, and forgotten false
  returns memory
actions.name: remember

refusals.message: Encounter content must not be blank.
This encounter was deleted; use a new save token for a new encounter.
This save token was already used for a different note.

actions.body:
where memory is not in Memories or memory.owner is not owner or memory.forgotten is true
then
  refuses REVISION_UNAVAILABLE "This encounter is not available."
where memory is in Memories and memory.owner is owner and memory.forgotten is not true and content is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_REVISION "Encounter content must not be blank."
where memory is in Memories and memory.owner is owner and memory.forgotten is not true and content is not blank
then
  replace memory.content with exact content and increment revision only when content changed, preserving capturedAt and identity
  leave an identical-content revision unchanged
  returns
actions.name: revise

refusals.message: This encounter is not available.
Encounter content must not be blank.

actions.body:
where memory is not in Memories or memory.owner is not owner
then
  refuses FORGET_NOT_OWNED "This encounter is not available."
where memory is in Memories and memory.owner is owner
then
  erase content and set forgotten true, retaining only metadata needed for safe retries
  increment revision when first forgotten; leave an already forgotten memory unchanged
  returns
actions.name: forget

refusals.message: This encounter is not available.

actions.body:
where audio is empty or malformed or mediaType is unsupported or the configured size limit is exceeded
then
  refuses INVALID_AUDIO "Provide a supported audio recording within the size limit."
where audio is valid and mediaType is supported and the configured size limit is not exceeded
then
  request transcription through the injectable server-configured provider using only the recording and media type
  bind the provider's transcript as content
  fail without changing Memories if the provider is unavailable or returns unusable output
  store no audio and create no memory; a repeated request can transcribe again
  returns content
actions.name: transcribe

refusals.message: Provide a supported audio recording within the size limit.

specification.principle: Sofia records meeting Toni at a seminar. She can retrieve the exact account later, correct what she wrote, or forget it. A transcription remains an editable draft until Sofia deliberately records it.
specification.purpose: Preserve an encounter account in its owner's words, including corrections and deliberate deletion, without treating an extracted interpretation as the account.

queries.body:
Answer exact content only for a live memory belonging to owner.
Answer no row for an unknown memory or another owner's memory or a forgotten memory.
queries.name: _get

queries.body:
Answer exact content and revision for a live owned memory, interpreting absent legacy revision as zero.
Answer no row for unknown, forgotten, or other-owner memory.
queries.name: _record

queries.body:
Answer only owner's live memories, including unindexed accounts and failed indexing attempts, at most 21 rows per page.
Answer no rows for an empty page or a nonempty cursor that is missing or not owned by owner; an empty cursor starts the first page.
Order by capturedAt descending then memory identity ascending; undated legacy memories follow dated memories in identity order, continuing strictly after the owned cursor.
queries.name: _list

state.body:
a set of Memories with
  an owner User
  an optional content String
  an optional capturedAt DateTime
  an optional submission String
  an optional revision Number
  an optional forgotten Flag

Rule: a new memory has identity derived from owner and submission. Separate submissions remain separate encounters even for identical names or content.
Rule: old memories without capturedAt or submission remain readable and editable. No clock time or encounter date is invented for old records.
Rule: capturedAt is the engine-supplied save instant, not the encounter date. Literal encounter context and optional Contact text remain in the exact account.
Rule: live memories have content and forgotten is not true; a metadata-only forgotten tombstone retains identity, owner and submission but no content or contact text. Legacy revision is zero. Every successful changed-content revision increments revision atomically.
Rule: remember atomically enforces owner-scoped submission uniqueness and conflicting-content refusal. revise and forget enforce ownership within the mutation itself.

concepts.name: RequestBoundary
concepts.principle: A call arrives and becomes pending. An answer travels back once; timeout or abort ends only the wait, while a quiescent interpreter failure returns an opaque internal error.
concepts.purpose: Let the outside world ask for things and receive answers, so each authored answer belongs to one pending call and failed waits settle without forging one.

concepts.name: Seeking
concepts.principle: Sofia records a robotics research goal, refines it, and sees it remain active across visits. Resolving it stops reconsideration; reopening starts it again. A search saved before ongoing goals existed also appears as an ongoing need, and she can resolve it with one action.
concepts.purpose: Keep a user's ongoing needs available for reconsideration until resolved, including searches saved before the lifecycle existed.

actions.body:
where description is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_DESCRIPTION "The need description must not be blank."
where description is not blank and at least one owned ongoing need has the same normalized description
then
  bind the matching ongoing need with smallest identity in ascending identity order as need
  preserve its original description, createdAt, active interpretation, and every existing duplicate record
  returns need
where description is not blank and no owned ongoing need has the same normalized description
then
  create need with a new UUID identity, owner, exact supplied description, supplied createdAt if any, and active true
  treat explicitly resolved needs as nonmatching even when their descriptions normalize identically
  returns need
actions.name: seek

refusals.message: The need description must not be blank.

actions.body:
where need is not in Needs or need.owner is not owner
then
  refuses NEED_REVISION_UNAVAILABLE "This goal is not available."
where need is in Needs and need.owner is owner and need.active is false
then
  refuses NEED_REVISION_INACTIVE "Reopen this goal before editing it."
where need is in Needs and need.owner is owner and need.active is not false and description is blank
then
  refuses EMPTY_NEED_REVISION "The need description must not be blank."
where need is in Needs and need.owner is owner and need.active is not false and description is not blank
then
  replace description and preserve need identity and createdAt
  leave an identical description unchanged
  returns
actions.name: revise

refusals.message: This goal is not available.
Reopen this goal before editing it.
The need description must not be blank.

actions.body:
where need is not in Needs or need.owner is not owner
then
  refuses NEED_RESOLUTION_UNAVAILABLE "This goal is not available."
where need is in Needs and need.owner is owner
then
  set active to false, leaving an already inactive need unchanged
  returns
actions.name: resolve

refusals.message: This goal is not available.

actions.body:
where need is not in Needs or need.owner is not owner
then
  refuses NEED_REOPEN_UNAVAILABLE "This goal is not available."
where need is in Needs and need.owner is owner
then
  set active to true, leaving an already active need unchanged
  returns
actions.name: reopen

refusals.message: This goal is not available.

actions.body:
where true
then
  atomically remove the need only when it belongs to owner
  leave an absent or other-owner need unchanged with the same successful result
  repeating deletion succeeds unchanged and can trigger owner-scoped downstream cleanup
  returns
actions.name: delete

specification.principle: Sofia records a robotics research goal, refines it, and sees it remain active across visits. Resolving it stops reconsideration; reopening starts it again. A search saved before ongoing goals existed also appears as an ongoing need, and she can resolve it with one action.
specification.purpose: Keep a user's ongoing needs available for reconsideration until resolved, including searches saved before the lifecycle existed.

queries.body:
Answer owner's need description.
Answer no row for an unknown need or another owner's need.

Rule: every new need has active true; application endpoints supply createdAt from the engine, while direct legacy invocations may omit it. A legacy need without active is interpreted as active and retains its original description and identity.
Rule: missing legacy createdAt remains unknown. Ordering never invents dates.
Rule: every mutation enforces owner membership within its atomic update. Unknown and other-owner needs have indistinguishable refusals or empty reads.
Rule: seek compares descriptions by trimming outer whitespace, collapsing each internal whitespace run to one space, and applying English-locale lowercase. Only normalized exact equality reuses a need; paraphrases are never merged. Legacy duplicate needs remain separate records.
Rule: reuse is guaranteed for sequential admitted invocations and the concept action queue in one assembly. Independent raw concurrent concept instances and multiple processes have no additional deduplication guarantee.

concepts.name: Sessioning
concepts.principle: After Maya proves who she is, a session is started for her. Each time she sends a request with the session, Sessioning returns her as the person it belongs to and records when she last used it. When she signs out, the session ends, and any later request that carries it is refused. She forgets to sign out on a library computer; nobody uses that session for a week, and then it is refused. She uses the session on her own laptop every day, but three months after it started, that one is refused too, and she signs in again.
concepts.purpose:
Let people stay signed in across requests without sending their password each time.

*Prevents:* someone keeps using a session after signing out; someone who finds a session left open on a shared computer, or copies one, keeps using it indefinitely; someone who comes back after a few days has to sign in again.

actions.body:
where true
then
  add a new session for subject, last used now, that expires 90 days from now
  returns session, expiresAt
actions.name: start

actions.body:
where session is unknown, has not been used for 7 days, or has expired
then
  refuses NOT_SIGNED_IN "Your session has ended. Sign in again."
where session was used within the last 7 days and has not expired
then
  set the session's lastUsed to now
  returns subject
actions.name: use

refusals.message: Your session has ended. Sign in again.

actions.body:

  returns session
actions.name: end

refusals.message: Your session has ended. Sign in again.

She uses the session on her own laptop every day, but three months after it started, that one is refused too, and she signs in again.

state.body:
a set of Connections with
  an owner User
  a target Target
  a need Need
  an evidence set of Evidence
  a reason String
  a gaps set of String
  an eligible Flag
  unique owner and need and target

a set of Exclusions with
  an owner User
  a target Target
  an explanation String
  unique owner and target

Rule: offer atomically enforces owner, need, target uniqueness. No target, need, or evidence identity is interpreted or merged by name. Legacy connection status fields have no meaning and never suppress otherwise eligible unexcluded suggestions.
Rule: exclusions apply to exact target identity for their owner across every need. They survive reset, clear, need revision, deletion, reopening, and repeat search. They are not note text, extraction facts, or shared learning.
Rule: every explanation has at most 1000 characters; the empty string means no explanation. All exclusions and explanations remain owner-private.
Rule: reset disables the prior set before recomputation; only successful offers reenable supported rows. An interrupted refresh cannot keep old rows eligible.
Rule: offer and all public suggestion queries enforce absence of an owner-target exclusion, including after provider completion; correctness never depends on clearing matching connection rows.
Rule: the injected recommendation policy is separate from evidence extraction. It receives only the supplied search description, candidate target, reason, gaps, and this owner's exclusion targets and explanations. It may reject a supported candidate but cannot invent candidates, alter evidence, or modify notes.
Rule: configured model policy uses a stateless strict boolean response, no retained provider response or shared conversation, and treats all supplied text as untrusted data. Missing, invalid, timed-out, or failed provider output faults explicitly without offering that candidate; there is no silent fallback or automatic retry. Local policy passes supported unexcluded candidates without a provider call.
Rule: policy context includes all owner exclusions in target identity ascending order with complete explanations. The complete serialized policy input is bounded to 128 KiB UTF-8; exceeding this budget faults explicitly before a provider call and never truncates feedback. Hard exclusion checks always use all owner exclusions. Exclusion saving is independent of this budget and succeeds without a policy call. No other owner's feedback can enter the policy call.
Rule: exclude and clear enforce ownership inside mutations; refusals leave complete state unchanged. Exclusion is durable before success is returned; a policy fault cannot erase it.

externalTypes.explanation: The account in the app that a sign-in on the other site reaches.
externalTypes.name: User

specification.principle: Sam starts a sign-in, approves the app on the other site, and his browser finishes the attempt it started. The other site confirms that the code belongs to its user `u7f3`, whose username is `sam`. The app registers `sam`, and his account `u7f3` is linked to that user. After he changes his username on the other site, Sam signs in again, and Federating returns the same user. Leo sends Sam a link that finishes a sign-in Leo started; Sam's browser never started that attempt, so finishing it is refused with "This sign-in has expired. Start again." Leo reads a code from Sam's browser history and finishes a sign-in of his own with it. The code was issued for the verifier of Sam's attempt, so the other site doesn't confirm it for Leo's, and finishing is refused with "The other site didn't confirm this sign-in. Start again."
specification.purpose:
Let people sign in with an account they already have on another site, and come back to the same account each time.

*Prevents:* someone opens a link that finishes a sign-in another person started, and ends up in that person's account; someone reads a code meant for another person, such as from their browser's history, and signs in as them; a person's details change on the other site, and they get a second account; someone links another person's account on the other site to an account they control.

queries.body: Returns the user linked to a confirmed attempt's subject, or no row when the attempt is unconfirmed or its subject is unlinked.
queries.name: _user

queries.body: Returns true when the attempt is confirmed, unexpired, and its subject unlinked, and false otherwise.
queries.name: _linkable

a set of Attempts with

  a verifier String
  an expiresAt DateTime

a set of Confirmed Attempts with

a set of Links with

Rule: an attempt, its nonce, and its verifier are unguessable. start returns the attempt and its nonce only to its caller, and finish refuses an attempt without its nonce. The verifier is sent only to the other site, with the code.
Rule: Federating may delete an attempt once it has expired.

a set of Sources with
  an owner User
  an optional contentDigest String
  an optional sourceRevision Number
  an optional observedAt DateTime
  an optional retracted Flag

a set of Entities with
  an owner User
  a kind EntityKind
  a label String

a set of Claims with

Rule: Sources retain owner and retraction metadata even after their claims are removed; a retracted source cannot be ingested again. ingest and retract enforce this atomically so an in-flight extraction cannot resurrect a forgotten source.
Rule: every claim and both endpoints have the same owner as its source. Every new quote is complete positive evidence from the exact indexed content, excluding guided Contact text.
Rule: every successful ingest records the SHA-256 digest of the exact supplied content before Contact exclusion. Legacy sources lacking that digest are not usable as current evidence until explicitly reindexed.
Rule: sourceRevision is monotone; an omitted revision is interpreted as zero for legacy direct calls and cannot replace a higher committed revision. An older in-flight ingest cannot replace a newer committed revision. observedAt is an engine-supplied processing instant, never an inferred encounter date; absent legacy instants remain unknown.
Rule: people remain local to their source, including equal names in different encounters. Only unambiguous exact normalized organization or topic identities may be shared across an owner's sources. Similar names or conflicting identity hints never cause a merge.
Rule: missing legacy usable means true; explicit false claims remain stored but are excluded from every trace and evidence query. Replacement removes old claims and resets extracted claims to usable, rather than transferring rejection to potentially different claims.

a set of Memories with
  an owner User
  an optional content String
  an optional capturedAt DateTime
  an optional submission String

Rule: a new memory has identity derived from owner and submission. Separate submissions remain separate encounters even for identical names or content.
Rule: old memories without capturedAt or submission remain readable and editable. No clock time or encounter date is invented for old records.
Rule: capturedAt is the engine-supplied save instant, not the encounter date. Literal encounter context and optional Contact text remain in the exact account.
Rule: live memories have content and forgotten is not true; a metadata-only forgotten tombstone retains identity, owner and submission but no content or contact text. Legacy revision is zero. Every successful changed-content revision increments revision atomically.
Rule: remember atomically enforces owner-scoped submission uniqueness and conflicting-content refusal. revise and forget enforce ownership within the mutation itself.

state.body:
a set of Needs with
  an owner User
  a description String
  an optional createdAt DateTime
  an optional active Flag

Rule: every new need has active true; application endpoints supply createdAt from the engine, while direct legacy invocations may omit it. A legacy need without active is interpreted as active and retains its original description and identity.
Rule: missing legacy createdAt remains unknown. Ordering never invents dates.
Rule: every mutation enforces owner membership within its atomic update. Unknown and other-owner needs have indistinguishable refusals or empty reads.
Rule: seek compares descriptions by trimming outer whitespace, collapsing each internal whitespace run to one space, and applying English-locale lowercase. Only normalized exact equality reuses a need; paraphrases are never merged. Legacy duplicate needs remain separate records.
Rule: reuse is guaranteed for sequential admitted invocations and the concept action queue in one assembly. Independent raw concurrent concept instances and multiple processes have no additional deduplication guarantee.

externalTypes.explanation: The person a session belongs to.
externalTypes.name: Subject

specification.principle: After Maya proves who she is, a session is started for her. Each time she sends a request with the session, Sessioning returns her as the person it belongs to and records when she last used it. When she signs out, the session ends, and any later request that carries it is refused. She forgets to sign out on a library computer; nobody uses that session for a week, and then it is refused. She uses the session on her own laptop every day, but three months after it started, that one is refused too, and she signs in again.
specification.purpose:
Let people stay signed in across requests without sending their password each time.

*Prevents:* someone keeps using a session after signing out; someone who finds a session left open on a shared computer, or copies one, keeps using it indefinitely; someone who comes back after a few days has to sign in again.

state.body:
a set of Sessions with
  a Subject
  a lastUsed DateTime
  an expiresAt DateTime

Rule: a session's identity is unguessable, and it is all a person sends to use the session.
Rule: Sessioning may delete a session at any time once it can no longer be used.
